key_insight: The paper shows that the best amount of reference guidance is not the longest successful prefix, but the prefix that best balances helping the model and preserving its own ability to generate a different correct trajectory.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive Reference Guidance (ARG) offers a practical way to improve reasoning-RL rollout quality within a fixed generation budget by reusing successful continuation outcomes to choose guidance prefixes.
method: Use prefix continuation: start from a verified reference prefix and let the model complete the trajectory.
Keep the model-generated rollout if it verifies; otherwise fall back to the reference solution.
Learn a shared prefix selector from continuation outcomes to adapt guidance without estimating success probabilities or generating extra samples.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, evaluated across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, ARG achieved the highest aggregate pass@12 with competitive average sampled accuracy.
watch_item: ARG still depends on verification and on the quality of continuation outcomes, so its gains may be sensitive to verifier reliability and the chosen generation budget.
paper_title: Balancing Reference Guidance and Free Generation in Trajectory Rollouts for Reasoning RL
